title: Enhancing Global Estimation of Fine Particulate Matter Concentrations by Including Geophysical a Priori Information in Deep Learning.
summary: The resulting global monthly PM2.5 estimates remain consistent with monitors under sparse training; at 1% of monitors, R² was 0.73 with geophysical inputs versus 0.51 without. The paper also reports spatial/seasonal distribution estimates. Buffer leave-one-out spatial cross-validation up to 1,000-km exclusion radii plus region/global monitor comparisons; R² 0.75–0.87 in global monthly spatial CV. It remains a model-derived estimate, with uncertainty and spatial/temporal autocorrelation caveats.
ai_technology: A residual CNN learns local bias in geophysical a priori PM2.5 using satellite, simulation and monitor inputs; a tailored loss constrains estimates in sparse-monitor regions.
organization: Department of Energy, Environmental, and Chemical Engineering, Washington University in St. Louis, St. Louis, Missouri 63130, United States

source_review.scope: Full primary ACS article reviewed (published online 2024-03-27). A residual CNN combines satellite, GEOS-Chem and monitor data to estimate monthly 1-km PM2.5 for 1998–2019, with a new buffer leave-one-out validation addressing spatial autocorrelation. Catalog checks found only distinct regional PM2.5 studies, no same global result.
